title: Deflating effective field theory
speaker: Adam Koberinski (Lund University)
description: UPAC Colloquium (Utrecht Philosophy of Astronomy & Cosmology): research presentation, no preparation needed. Hybrid; the Teams link goes out via the upac-l mailing list. To join the speaker for dinner, e-mail cosmo-master.assistant@uu.nl the day before.
abstract: Inflationary effective field theory (EFT) provides a unified framework for a wide class of inflationary models. But should it be understood as a mere phenomenological parameterization, or as a physically principled theory in the richer sense associated with EFTs in particle physics? We argue that inflationary EFT occupies an uncomfortable middle position: it carries more theoretical commitments than a purely phenomenological framework warrants, yet fails to meet several structural conditions characteristic of other EFTs—stable scale separation, naturalness, and well-defined successor relations. We identify three sources of difficulty: intrinsic limitations of the framework (it cannot describe the onset or end of inflation), top-down tensions with quantum gravity, and bottom-up naturalness problems afflicting empirically favoured models. Attempts to exploit these tensions as a window onto UV physics require significant revision to standard inflationary EFT.
